text: Given a valid token, listing accounts with no filters returns accounts with id/name/status/created_at, defaulting to at most 50 results.
Given more than 200 accounts exist (mocked), requesting limit=200 returns at most 200.
Given a known account id, getting that account returns its detail.
Given an unknown account id, getting that account returns a structured not_found error, not a crash.
Given a valid token, listing domains with no account filter returns every domain visible to that manager.
Given a valid token and an account id, listing domains scoped to that account returns only that account's domains.
Given a known domain id, getting that domain returns its detail.
Given an unknown domain id, getting that domain returns a structured not_found error.
Given a valid token and a new domain name, creating that domain returns the created domain's detail including a generated id.
Given a domain-create call where the manager's token lacks permission (mocked 403), the tool returns a structured unauthorized error.
Given a domain id and a date range, the traffic report returns the blocked/spam/delivered counts and a per-user breakdown for that range.
Given a domain id, listing user groups returns each group's name, service list, and user count.
Given a user-group id, listing users returns only users in that group.
Given a domain id, listing users (no group filter) returns every user under that domain.
Given a known user id, getting that user returns its detail.
Given an unknown user id, getting that user returns a structured not_found error.
Given a domain id and a new username, creating a user returns the created user with a generated id and default group.
Given user_type=alias without a parent_id, creating that user returns a structured invalid_argument error.
Given an existing user id and a different group id, moving that user succeeds and is confirmed.
Given an existing user id, deleting that user succeeds and is confirmed.
Given an unknown user id, deleting that user returns not_found, not a silent success.
Given a domain id, a date range, and direction=inbound, the message-stats tool returns only inbound per-user summaries.
Given a domain id with one allow rule and one block rule, listing with rule_type=block returns only the block rule.
Given a domain id, adding one block rule and then listing the rules shows it present.
Given a domain id, calling the remove path with an empty rules list is rejected by the tool itself before any call reaches the vendor's destroy-rules endpoint.
steps: Start the service locally with a mocked api_client fixture pre-loaded with two rules
Observe the tool's response and the mocked client's call log
expect: The tool returns an invalid_argument error and the mocked client records zero calls to the destroy-rules endpoint
notes: Design-time ledger; dev leg executes and fills result/evidence.

text: Given a domain id, getting spam tolerance returns the effective thresholds and which entity they are inherited from.
Given a domain id, setting new spam-tolerance thresholds and then getting them again reflects the change.
Given a domain id with custom thresholds already set, resetting and then getting again shows the thresholds reverted to inherited.
Given possible_spam_max_score < possible_spam_min_score, setting spam tolerance returns a structured invalid_argument error before any call reaches the vendor API.
Given an account id, getting settings returns the effective settings list.
Given an account id and one named setting, setting it and then getting settings again reflects the new value.
Given a valid token, getting dashboard stats returns the manager-scoped summary data.
Given two simulated concurrent requests carrying two different X-Mailprotector-Auth-Token values, processing them concurrently results in each response reflecting only its own token.
Given a request to /mcp with no X-Mailprotector-Auth-Token header, the response is 401 and the body lists the required header, before any outbound call to Mailprotector.
Given a real Mailprotector manager token, running initialize -> tools/list -> tools/call for mailprotector_list_domains against the live API returns a well-formed result.
steps: Obtain a real manager auth token from whoever owns a Mailprotector demo/test account
Run the service locally with that token in X-Mailprotector-Auth-Token
Call initialize, then tools/list, then tools/call mailprotector_list_domains
expect: tools/list shows 20 tools; tools/call returns 200 with a well-formed domain list (or an empty list if the test account has none)
notes: Needs a real vendor account; not available at design time. Per references/mcp-track.md section 3, this does not block delivery.
